Re-measured by hand rather than re-read: the digest still joins only at a stated recipe (both recipes agree on the ordinary fixture, so a consumer records what a no-index fetch would have produced), and the cross-implementation check is what makes 'at a stated recipe' mean something rather than each side agreeing only with a frozen constant of its own. Refs now carry the SYMBOL NAME beside the line, so the next growth costs a grep instead of a re-derivation.

The two layers are now visible side by side: `repomd.json::files[*].sha256` is written from per-file digests in the writer (memory.rs:221 and the sibling inserts through :285), carries no recipe and needs none because it covers our own bytes at rest; the per-entry `content_hash` carries `sha256-tree/1:` because it covers foreign package content that a second implementation must be able to recompute by the same rule. Independence re-checked, not assumed: nothing in the writer derives one from the other.
